---
title: Ways to define terms
description: Define glossary entries in a document's front matter, in one or more YAML or JSON files, or in both.
---

Entries can come from three places. The extension reads all of them, checks
for duplicate keys, and treats the result as one vocabulary.

| Where | Option | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| The document's [[front-matter]] | `glossary.entries` | One self-contained document, a handout, a demo |
| One [[yaml|short]] or [[json|short]] file | `glossary.path: glossary.yml` | A paper, a thesis, a course |
| Several files | `glossary.path: [a.yml, b.yml]` | Shared vocabularies split by topic |
: Sources of glossary entries. {#tbl-sources}

## In the front matter

The whole vocabulary can live inside the document. No other file is needed:

```yaml
---
title: Reading a confidence interval
filters: [glossary]
glossary:
  entries:
    - id: se
      kind: acronym
      short: SE
      long: standard error
      definition: The standard deviation of an estimate across repeated samples.

    - id: sample-mean
      term: sample mean
      plural: sample means
      symbol: $\bar{x}$
      definition: The average of the observed values in one sample.
---

The [[se]] of the [[sample-mean]] shrinks as the sample grows.

::: {.glossary}
:::
```

Entries take the same fields as in a file. See the
[field reference](reference.qmd#term-fields). The
[confidence-interval lesson](demos/front-matter.qmd) is built this way and
renders to both HTML and PDF.

## In one file

Point `path` at a YAML or JSON file with an `entries` list:

```yaml
filters: [glossary]
glossary:
  path: glossary.yml
```

```yaml
# glossary.yml
entries:
  - id: sample-size
    term: sample size
    plural: sample sizes
    symbol: $n$
    definition: The number of units included in an analysis.

  - id: doi
    kind: acronym
    short: DOI
    long: digital object identifier
    short-plural: DOIs
    definition: A persistent identifier for a digital object.
```

When `glossary` has neither `path` nor `entries`, the extension looks for
`glossary.yml`. Relative paths are resolved against the project directory
first and then against the document's directory.

The JSON form uses the same field names:

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {"id": "doi", "kind": "acronym", "short": "DOI",
     "long": "digital object identifier",
     "definition": "A persistent identifier for a digital object."}
  ]
}
```

## In several files

`path` also accepts a list. The files are read in order:

```yaml
glossary:
  path:
    - statistics.yml
    - acronyms.yml
    - course-2026.json
```

A key defined in two places stops the render and names both:

```console
glossary: duplicate glossary id 'se' in statistics.yml and acronyms.yml
```

## Files plus page terms

`path` and `entries` combine. Use this when a lecture needs a few terms that
the shared vocabulary does not:

```yaml
glossary:
  path: course.yml
  entries:
    - id: bootstrap
      term: bootstrap
      definition: Resampling the data with replacement to estimate the
        variability of a statistic.
```

Set `path: false` to load no file at all, for example when the project
default should not apply to one page.

## Websites and books

Put the shared options in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
filters: [glossary]
glossary:
  path: glossary.yml
  html-glossary-page: glossary.qmd
```

Create `glossary.qmd` with a placeholder that lists every entry:

```markdown
---
title: Glossary
---

::: {.glossary include-unused="true"}
:::
```

References on every other page then link to that page. A page with its own
placeholder keeps its links on the page. This manual uses exactly this setup.

::: {.callout-important title="A page's glossary block replaces the project's"}
Quarto merges project and page metadata key by key. When a page sets its own
`glossary:` block, that block replaces the one in `_quarto.yml`. It is not
merged with it. A page that adds `entries` must repeat any project options it
still needs:

```yaml
glossary:
  path: glossary.yml
  html-glossary-page: glossary.qmd
  entries:
    - id: bootstrap
      term: bootstrap
      definition: Resampling the data with replacement.
```

The [demo lesson](demos/front-matter.qmd) relies on this: its own
`glossary:` block drops the manual's vocabulary file and glossary page.
:::

## Older schemas

For vocabularies written for other tools, `key` or `label` work as `id`,
`name` as `term`, `description` as `definition`, `abbreviation` or `acronym`
as `short`, and `expansion` as `long`. A file may also use a `terms` list or
groups of rows (`groups[].rows`) in place of `entries`.
